_: Mutations the covering test does NOT catch. May only SHRINK. Each needs a reason.

survivors.coaching/postRaceRecoveryCurve.test.ts :: EQUIVALENT, proved by reading: `raceWeekN >= plan.weeks.length` is an early return, and when it is skipped the very next guard `windowEnd < raceWeekN + 1` evaluates to the identical condition (with no following race, windowEnd IS plan.weeks.length). Both paths return null for the same inputs. The first guard is a cheap early exit, not a distinct rule; nothing a test can observe distinguishes them.

EQUIVALENT, proved by the caller contract: idx comes from `findIndex((w, i) => i + 1 > raceWeekN && ...)`, so a hit at index 0 would need raceWeekN < 1. raceWeekN is 1-indexed and every caller passes >= 1, so idx is never 0 when found and `>= 0` and `> 0` cannot differ. Would stop being equivalent if a caller ever passed 0 — which would be its own defect.
survivors.coaching/prompts/sessionFeedback.test.ts: EQUIVALENT: mutates the 86_400_000 in `days = Math.round((now - raceDate) / 86_400_000)`. One millisecond on a day-length divisor moves a 21-day result to 20.99999, which Math.round returns as 21. The output is integer days; the mutation cannot reach it.
survivors.coaching/readinessBaseline.test.ts :: fl: EQUIVALENT THROUGH THIS API. `today.hrvMs <= hrvBaseline - (HRV_DECLINE_SD * hrvSd)` uses the UNROUNDED sample SD, while `detail.hrvSd` is rounded to 2dp — so the edge a caller can reconstruct (54.81 on the test window) is not the edge the engine used (54.8113...). `<=` and `<` differ only on that exact float, which no runner's HRV lands on and no public value can address. The boundary BEHAVIOUR is pinned either side of the edge in readinessBaseline.test.ts.
survivors.coaching/reshapeMagnitude.test.ts :: fli: EQUIVALENT: `kind === 'modified' || (before && after)` only widens entry to the branch for kinds that reach L82 at all, and replaced/added/removed all return 'high' at L79 first. The only other kind is 'unchanged', which computeSessionDiff builds with label, distance AND duration equal — so the distance comparison inside yields 0% and returns the same 'low'.

EQUIVALENT, proved at the producer: computeSessionDiff (lib/coaching/diff/sessionDiff.ts:101) constructs kind 'modified' only as `{ before: bb, after: aa }` with both non-null. `before && after` is therefore always true for a 'modified' entry, and `before || after` is too.
